root_cause.text: The x86 APIC resume path in `lapic_resume()` assumed firmware would preserve the kernel’s APIC mode across s2ram, so when firmware silently re-enabled x2APIC while `x2apic_mode` was already set to 0, the kernel kept using the xAPIC interface against x2APIC hardware state, leading to hangs.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds a check in `arch/x86/kernel/apic/apic.c` during `lapic_resume()` that, in the `else` branch for `x2apic_mode == 0`, tests `x2apic_enabled()` and explicitly calls `__x2apic_disable()` with a warning `"x2apic: re-enabled by firmware during resume. Disabling"`, and the CVE description states the bug occurs because firmware may re-enable x2apic on resume even though the kernel had disabled it earlier, causing the kernel to continue using xapic while hardware is in x2apic mode.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a no-op x2APIC disable stub for non-x2APIC builds so callers can invoke it safely regardless of configuration.
intent_record.what: A new empty static inline function named `__x2apic_disable(void)` was added to the `#ifndef CONFIG_X86_X2APIC` stub section, alongside the existing no-op stubs for `try_to_enable_x2apic(int remap_mode)` and `__x2apic_enable(void)`.
intent_record.how: This makes `__x2apic_disable()` available as a no-op when x2APIC support is not compiled in, allowing code that calls this helper to build and link unconditionally without needing additional preprocessor guards.

intent_record.intent_summary: Detect and disable x2APIC if firmware re-enables it during resume while restoring legacy APIC mode.
intent_record.what: In the non-x2APIC resume path of `lapic_resume()`, a new check was added: if `x2apic_enabled()` returns true, the code now logs a one-time warning and calls `__x2apic_disable()` before continuing with the existing APICBASE setup logic.
intent_record.how: During resume, if firmware has unexpectedly turned x2APIC back on while the kernel is resuming in legacy APIC mode, the kernel now detects that state, warns once, and disables x2APIC so the subsequent APICBASE reinitialization proceeds with the expected mode.

grouping_result.intent: Add a no-op x2APIC disable stub for non-x2APIC builds so callers can invoke it safely regardless of configuration.
Detect and disable x2APIC if firmware re-enables it during resume while restoring legacy APIC mode.

relevance_review.reason: The change only adds a no-op disable stub for non-x2APIC builds. It does not address the APIC resume path bug where firmware could re-enable x2APIC during s2ram and the kernel would fail to reconcile hardware state with x2apic_mode in lapic_resume().

The change directly matches the root cause: it handles the resume path where firmware may silently re-enable x2APIC and ensures the kernel detects this state and disables x2APIC/keeps APIC mode consistent, preventing the xAPIC-vs-x2APIC mismatch that caused hangs.

candidates.rationale: This conditional assumes the kernel's cached x2APIC state is authoritative during resume. When firmware silently re-enables x2APIC while x2apic_mode is 0, execution falls into the legacy APIC path and the kernel continues using the wrong interface, which is the core of the hang.

This is the only pre-fix action that restores x2APIC, but it is guarded solely by x2apic_mode. Because the code does not detect firmware having re-enabled x2APIC independently, the resume logic can skip this despite hardware being in x2APIC mode.

vuln_statements.explanation: This guard makes the resume path depend only on the kernel's cached x2APIC mode. If firmware silently re-enabled x2APIC during s2ram while x2apic_mode is 0, the code would skip the x2APIC re-enable path and continue with the wrong APIC interface.

This is the action that restores x2APIC, but it is only reached when the stale x2apic_mode flag is set. The vulnerable behavior is that resume can miss this re-enable step even though hardware has already been switched back to x2APIC by firmware.

x86/x2apic: Split enable and setup function

enable_x2apic() is a convoluted unreadable mess because it is used for

bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit 659006bf3ae37a08706907ce1a36ddf57c9131d2
Author: Thomas Gleixner <tglx@kernel.org>
Date:   Thu Jan 15 21:22:26 2015 +0000

    x86/x2apic: Split enable and setup function
    
    enable_x2apic() is a convoluted unreadable mess because it is used for
    both enablement in early boot and for setup in cpu_init().
    
    Split the code into x2apic_enable() for enablement and x2apic_setup()
    for setup of (secondary cpus). Make use of the new state tracking to
    simplify the logic.
bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable resume-path behavior described in the root cause is not present in this snippet. In `lapic_resume()`, the code now distinguishes the x2APIC case and calls `__x2apic_enable()` directly: `if (x2apic_mode) { __x2apic_enable(); } else { ... }`. The new helper `__x2apic_enable()` explicitly checks MSR state and only writes `X2APIC_ENABLE` if it is not already set: `rdmsrl(MSR_IA32_APICBASE, msr); if (msr & X2APIC_ENABLE) return; wrmsrl(..., msr | X2APIC_ENABLE);`. This is the corrective logic that avoids assuming the previous APIC mode handling and ensures x2APIC is re-enabled when needed after resume. The old problematic path of calling `enable_x2apic()` from resume is gone, so the vulnerable construct is absent and the fix is present.
